title: Rollout Orbit dashboard and shadow-traffic harmonizer
creator: Aisha Kumari
description: Goal: Deliver a lightweight, operator-friendly dashboard ("Rollout Orbit") that surfaces per-route rollout health, provides side-by-side variant comparisons, links traces/downstream requests, and includes a shadow-traffic harmonizer that streamlines shadow routing and sampling. This ticket scopes the initial MVP (APIs + Console pages + telemetry plumbing) to enable fast canaries, A/B experiments, shadow playback, and deterministic auto-rollback triggers for model-serving rollouts. Success = teams can detect regressions within 5 minutes of starting a canary, run a 10% shadow sample with preconfigured capture, and configure a single auto-rollback policy that triggers within configured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Rollout Orbit dashboard page exists under Console > Deployments and shows active rollouts with per-route metrics (p50,p95,median latency, error rate, request throughput, token-cost) updated no slower than 30s.
Side-by-side variant comparison view: selectable baseline vs candidate with normalized metric deltas and visual sparkline overlays for the selected window.
Trace linking: each anomalous bucket includes direct links to related traces in supported tracing systems (Jaeger/Datadog) and a 1-click open to the request inspector.
Shadow-traffic harmonizer UI: per-route toggle to enable shadowing, configurable sample rate (0.1% - 50%), and an opt-in sticky sampling mode. Changes take effect without a console restart.

Auto-rollback policy editor: users can create policies based on metric thresholds and divergence signals (latency p95 > baseline + X ms for Y mins OR error-rate delta > Z%) and policies can be toggled on/off per-rollout.
Backend: telemetry pipeline supports a 'rollout_id' tag, variant label, and shadow flag. Aggregation keys are per-route, per-variant, and time-bucket.
Telemetry storage window default 7 days with export-as-CSV for the selected time window.
Docs: Console doc + runbook published with examples and a 'how to recover' section for false-positives.
E2E: Smoke test that creates a canary, drives synthetic traffic, observes expected metric delta, and validates auto-rollback fires when policy breached (in sandbox).
tasks: PM: finalize metric set and acceptance thresholds (this ticket)
Design: deliver Figma mocks for Rollout Orbit overview + variant compare (deadline 2025-02-18)
Backend: extend telemetry producer to attach rollout_id + variant + shadow flag; add clickhouse aggregate table + materialized view
Backend: implement auto-rollback evaluation service that consumes aggregated signals and emits rollback events to rollout-orchestrator
Frontend: implement Rollout Orbit page and Variant Compare modal; reuse existing chart components where possible
Infra: add sampling control path for shadow traffic at the router level and ensure 95th percentile sampling stability
QA: create synthetic traffic harness and automated tests for canary -> rollback flow
Docs: draft Console docs and incident runbook; include sample policies and troubleshooting tips
decisions: Metric set: start with latency (p50/p95), error rate, and model-output divergence (embedding cosine on canonical promptset) — avoids early inclusion of token-cost until UI bandwidth available.
Trace linking: surface links to existing tracing backends (Datadog/Jaeger) via stored trace_id; do not ship embedded trace viewer in MVP to limit scope.
Shadow sampling: default to 5% sample for new rollouts; expose override in UI. Sampling uses hash-based deterministic sampling keyed by request id to keep comparisons stable.
Auto-rollback: use a rule engine evaluating sliding windows (default 5m). Rollback events will be 'suggested' by default; a customer with Dedicated/Enterprise can enable automated enforcement.
Storage: keep 7-day hot window in ClickHouse + 30-day cold archive in object storage for cost control.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Embedding-based divergence provides a fast signal of semantic drift but is compute-heavy; we'll run divergence on a sampled promptset and surface as a 'divergence score' rather than raw vectors.

Keeping trace viewer out of MVP reduces frontend scope but requires users to switch contexts to debug — mitigated by deep-links into tracing tools and a 'capture sample' feature that pushes golden traces to the tracing backend.
High-cardinality label explosion risk: keep aggregation keys minimal (route, variant, shadow) for the default view; expose finer granularity in advanced filters.

Auto-rollback automation increases risk of flapping in noisy workloads; include cooldown windows and require two consecutive windows of breach before enforced rollback unless user chooses aggressive mode.
